description: We are S3L, research based team, our main goal is to create SI-based dashboard for predicting, explaining and preventing fire-based hazards. Our skills consist of technical development, IT-work, coding, analytics, graphic design and management.
summary:
KOPALA is a fire detection and analysis software project developed by team S3L. It connects camera-based detection with scientific data analysis to help users identify potential flames and better understand combustion behavior.

Our prototype uses computer vision to highlight suspected flames in a camera view. Alongside detection, interactive analysis tools explore NASA combustion datasets, including FLEX liquid-droplet experiments. Users can investigate how fuel type, droplet diameter, oxygen concentration, and pressure relate to burn duration, with comparisons that account for experimental conditions.

We aim to combine these capabilities with machine learning and an AI explanation layer that translates analytical results into clear language supported by graphs and mathematical relationships. Explanations should distinguish measured evidence from predictions and communicate uncertainty.

Although NASA research provides a scientific foundation, KOPALA focuses on general fire detection and analysis, with potential applications in research, education, and supplementary monitoring. Future work includes broader datasets, model validation, and testing under varied lighting and environmental conditions.

KOPALA is currently a prototype, not a certified fire alarm. Our mission is to make fire information more accessible by connecting detection, analysis, and understanding in one platform.
